title: Successor Desk Note: Base Count for the Successor Response Window When a Sale Is Under Way in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Rule.** For the successor's notices on a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case on a Cedarline Summit loan reclassified to the death of the last surviving borrower, the base count is set by the sale already under way on the case:

- **Supported sale or retention.** Where the case carries a received extension request supported by a listing agreement or a financing commitment, and the most recent accepted intent declaration on the case declares a sale or a retention of the property, the base count is 21 days.
- **Declared only.** Where that declaration declares a sale or a retention but the case carries no such request, the base count is 25 days.
- **Otherwise.** The base count is the death plan's successor response days, which is 30 under the Death of Last Surviving Borrower plan.

**Most recent declaration.** Among accepted intent declarations made on the same day, the most recent is the one recorded later by its recorded date and time.

## Truth table

| Received extension request backed by a listing agreement or financing commitment | Most recent accepted declaration | Base count |
|---|---|---|
| yes | sell or retain | 21 days |
| no | sell or retain | 25 days |
| yes or no | deed in lieu, or none on the case | 30 days (death plan's successor response days) |

## Hypothetical illustration

A case carries an extension request still awaiting a decision, backed by a listing agreement. Its only accepted declaration is of a deed in lieu. The declaration is neither a sale nor a retention, so the base count is 30 days.
